title: Sky keeps its own relayer alongside Keel's on the same Liquidity Layer contracts, and a separate Freezer holds the stop
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.1.1.1.2.1.4 states that the Relayer Role on Ethereum is held by two multisigs — "Prime Relayer Multisig" and "Core Operator Relayer Multisig" — and the Solana equivalent (…2.2.7) names three, including a Core Operator Relayer. A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.1.2.2.1 confirms the first "has the `RELAYER_ROLE`... and is controlled by Keel." A separate Freezer Multisig holds the freeze authority on each chain (…2.1.3, …2.2.6).

Two separations are in play. The first is *who may act*: Sky Core keeps an operator with live relayer privileges on an Agent's own liquidity layer, so the Agent is not the sole party able to move its positions. Operational continuity survives an Agent that goes dark, and Sky is not reduced to governance-speed remedies when transaction-speed action is required.

The second is *who may stop*: freezing is not a strong form of relaying but a distinct role in a distinct multisig. Whoever can halt the system is deliberately not whoever runs it, so an operator that misbehaves cannot also suppress the response — the classic separation between the accelerator and the brake.

The cost is a broadened attack surface. Every additional privileged multisig is another key set that can be compromised, which is why the rate limits sit in a contract that binds all relayers equally regardless of which one is acting.
description: The RELAYER_ROLE is held by both a Keel-controlled Prime Relayer Multisig and a Core Operator Relayer Multisig, while a distinct Freezer Multisig holds the halt authority on each chain.
